topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecturer's introduction, course context, and the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer and the Balance Between Intrinsic and Environmental Causes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual framework of cancer development, weighing intrinsic cellular errors and bad luck against environmental exposures and epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogenesis of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological pathogens drive oncogenesis, focusing on the discovery and mechanisms of Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Carcinogens and Metabolic DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how dietary toxins, radiation, and chemical exposures undergo host metabolic processing to form mutagenic DNA adducts and lesions.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of tumorigenesis, including the role of promoters, chronic inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental tissue susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine whether agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing and final summary on evaluating everyday carcinogen risks versus benefits.
